fields.description:
# Enforce the 50/72 commit-message rule with a local commit-msg hook

## Context / Problem

Gerrit renders a change description as preformatted text and preserves the author's newlines, so the wrapping a commit lands with is exactly what reviewers read (and what `git log` shows in an 80-column terminal). Gerrit's bundled `commit-message-length-validator` only WARNS (`warning: subject >50 characters`, `warning: too many message lines longer than 72 characters; manually wrap lines`), which is trivially ignored — and nothing in this repo checked it.

Result: commit bodies on `main` are split between hard-wrapped (72-79 col) and single-paragraph (129-286 col) styles. Measured with the new checker against the last 40 commits on origin/main: 5 pass, 35 fail, with failures like 177, 183, 222 and 223-char body lines. That inconsistency is what made the wrapping look like something rebar was doing to the text (investigated under ticket 368a, closed not_a_bug).

Research basis — all four major Gerrit-based projects mandate the same rule, and none avoids the line breaks:
- Go: "The text should be wrapped at around 72 columns" + "Don't use HTML, Markdown, or any other markup language."
- Chromium: "Long lines should be wrapped to 72 columns for easier log message viewing in terminals."
- ChromiumOS: "Wrap the body text to 72 characters so that `git log` looks nice"; subject ~60, 72 hard limit.
- Android: "Provide a long description that hard-wraps at 72 characters maximum"; subject 50 max.

## Approach

Enforce locally at commit time (operator's explicit choice: pre-commit framework, NOT CI).

- `scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py` — check-only checker for the 50/72 rule, matching the repo's existing `scripts/check_*.py` convention. Never rewrites the message; it names the offending lines.
- Wired as a `commit-message-wrap` hook in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` at the **commit-msg** stage. It cannot run at the `pre-commit` stage because the commit message does not exist yet. `default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg]` installs both.
- `make hooks` now verifies BOTH hooks landed AND that Gerrit's Change-Id stamping survived.

Carve-outs (wrapping these would break them): trailers (`rebar-ticket:`, `Change-Id:`, `Signed-off-by:`), `TAG=` lines, fenced code blocks, indented literal blocks, table rows, and lines whose length comes from a single unsplittable atomic token (URL, path, dotted identifier). Comment lines and the `git commit --verbose` diff are ignored.

## Critical risk handled: Gerrit's commit-msg hook

Gerrit's own `commit-msg` hook (which stamps `Change-Id`) already owns that slot. `pre-commit install` defaults to MIGRATION mode, preserving the existing hook as `commit-msg.legacy` and running both. Verified empirically in a throwaway repo: a conforming commit still received its `Change-Id`; an over-long body was rejected and no commit was created. `pre-commit install -f/--overwrite` would delete Gerrit's hook and break every push — documented as a do-not-do in the config, the Makefile, and CONTRIBUTING.md, and `make hooks` warns if the Change-Id chain is missing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A commit whose body has a line over 72 columns is REJECTED locally, with output naming each offending line and its length.
- [ ] A commit whose subject exceeds 50 columns is REJECTED locally.
- [ ] A conforming commit succeeds AND still receives its Gerrit `Change-Id` trailer (Gerrit's hook is chained as `commit-msg.legacy`, not clobbered).
- [ ] A body line is EXEMPT from the 72-column check when any of these detection rules matches (each stated as the exact rule an executor implements):
  - [ ] **Trailer** — the stripped line matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:\s` (e.g. `rebar-ticket:`, `Change-Id:`, `Signed-off-by:`).
  - [ ] **Tag** — the stripped line matches `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=` (e.g. `BUG=`, `TEST=`).
  - [ ] **Fenced block** — the line lies between two lines matching `^\s*```{3}`; the fence marker TOGGLES, so prose after a closing fence is checked again.
  - [ ] **Indented literal block** — the RAW line begins with exactly 4+ spaces or a tab, i.e. `line.startswith(("    ", "\t"))`. A 1-3 space indent is NOT exempt.
  - [ ] **Table row** — the stripped line begins with `|`.
  - [ ] **Atomic token** — the line contains a whitespace-delimited token longer than 72 chars, EVERY such over-long token matches `://|[/\\]|\w[._-]\w` (a URL scheme, a path separator, or a dotted/underscored/hyphenated identifier), AND the rest of the stripped line (its length minus the longest such token) is itself <= 72. A 73+ char run of ordinary characters is NOT exempt.
- [ ] git's own scaffolding produces no false positives: comment (`#`) lines and the `git commit --verbose` diff below the `>8` marker are ignored.
- [ ] The checker never mutates the commit message (check-only, matching the repo's stated pre-commit policy).
- [ ] `.pre-commit-config.yaml` gains a top-level `default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg]` key, so the EXISTING bare `pre-commit install` in `make hooks` (which passes no `--hook-type`) installs both hook types with no flag change.
- [ ] The `hooks:` target in `Makefile` is MODIFIED to add the two new verification branches described below; it currently verifies only the `pre-commit` hook file and must not be left as-is.
- [ ] `make hooks` EXITS NON-ZERO when either the `pre-commit` or the `commit-msg` hook file is absent after install.
- [ ] `make hooks` prints a WARNING (and still exits zero) when no `Change-Id` stamping is found in `commit-msg` or `commit-msg.legacy`, since Gerrit's hook is fetched separately and its absence must not block wiring the local gates.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md documents the enforcement, the exemption list, why the hook runs at the commit-msg stage, and the never-run-`pre-commit install -f` warning.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the rule, every carve-out, the fence-toggle case, and the CLI exit codes.

## Notes / scope

Local guardrail only — bypassable with `git commit --no-verify`, and CI does NOT check wrapping (deliberate: the operator chose pre-commit over CI). Existing history is not rewritten; the gate applies to new commits only.
